Figure_1.title: A measured reagent swap reverses with the substrate and must be learned, not copied
Figure_1.legend: Replacing PdCl₂(dtbpf) (X) with PdCl₂(PPh₃)₂ (Y) raises the Suzuki yield of 6-bromoquinoline with 4-methoxyphenylboronic acid from 4.98% to 93.36% under Cs₂CO₃. Copying this change to the related 5-bromo-1H-indazole predicts a gain, but the measured yield falls from 83.86% to 11.55%. The strip shows the same substitution across all 448 substrate pairs (blue, gain; red, loss); rings mark the two examples. Across nineteen arrays, the signs of 271 of 283 testable swaps cannot be reproduced by one preferred direction per substrate pair and one per recipe background (Fig. 2). Learning instead relates a two-well reference to its target through historical reactions in the same arrays. For held-out targets whose own substrate pair was measured in another recipe background, copying that reference changes prediction error by +42.4% relative to history alone, whereas learning changes it by −13.7% (Fig. 3). Labels with reference numbers mark where condition recommendation, general-conditions searches, transfer learning and yield-change prediction act on this decision. Orange denotes copying and teal learning.

Figure_2.title: Substitution responses depend jointly on substrate and recipe background
Figure_2.legend: **a**, Responses to PdCl₂(dtbpf) → PdCl₂(PPh₃)₂ for 412 substrate pairs measured under both Cs₂CO₃ and K₂CO₃; 145 have opposite signs (shaded quadrants; Pearson r = 0.55). Examples 1 (5-bromo-1H-indazole) and 2 (2-bromo-3-methoxypyridine) are drawn below the plot with their measured yields. Their three negative responses and one positive response cannot all be reproduced by multiplying one sign per substrate pair by one sign per background. **b**, Conflicting and testable swaps in each of nineteen arrays, using all nonzero changes (circles) or changes of at least 20 points (diamonds); totals are 271/283 and 143/212. A swap is testable when its observed pair-background graph contains a cycle. **c**, Complete response distributions for one exact substitution in each of six transformations. The Suzuki distribution contains 448 substrate pairs for the flagship substitution. Every point is a measured pair; blue and red denote positive and negative changes.

Figure_3.title: Historical relationships make the same reference measurements useful
Figure_3.legend: **a**, Two reference wells measured for the target substrate pair in another recipe background (top) are either copied or related to the target through historical reactions. Prediction-error changes relative to history alone are shown for seventeen screens and the hierarchical group average (Overall); screens are ordered by learned error change. Overall changes are +42.4% for copying and −13.7% for learning. The arrow marks a copied-error value beyond the plotted range. The inset counts missed or wrong directions among 21,997 held-out changes of at least 20 points: 18.6 per hundred for copying and 13.6 for learning; zero predictions count as missed directions. **b**, Reference and target responses for 452 training pairs in an amide-coupling additive substitution, pentafluorophenol → N-hydroxyphthalimide. The orange line copies at unit slope; the teal line shows the learned predictor at mean reference activity. **c**, Error removed by a reference for the same substitution relative to a matched control substitution. Grey points denote screens and teal points hierarchical group averages; rows give the held-out object and the fraction of historical training data (25% or 100%). Orange denotes copying and teal learning.

Figure_4.title: Measured alternatives and local profiles guide the next reagent choice
Figure_4.legend: **a**, Moving methylthio from meta to para lowers the HBTU/no-HOBt amide yield from 91.34% to 0.00%; TPTU without HOBt gives 92.79% for the para isomer. The network joins recipes differing in one slot, with DIPEA, DMF, 25 °C and 2 h fixed. **b**, Twelve Suzuki yields before and after boronic-acid methyl relocation. Under K₃PO₄, PdCl₂(PCy₃)₂ falls from 47.62% to 0.00%; SPhos Pd G3 gives 92.48% after relocation. Halos mark relocated groups; red outlines denote failure and blue outlines measured alternatives. Yields are shown to two decimals. **c**, Shared-scope conflicts resolved by measured alternatives in each transformation: 285 of 542 overall, with 257 unresolved. Within the resolved subset, 266, 16 and 3 conflicts require one, two and three additional options, respectively. **d**, Error change from adding history to the same local profiles for 24,221 queries. Profile counts and endpoint-well ranges are shown on the horizontal axis. Eight profiles (48–240 endpoint wells here) give a 9.7% improvement over profiles alone.

Extended_Data_Figure_1.title: Exact substitutions span nineteen reaction arrays
Extended_Data_Figure_1.legend: Bars give exact substitution counts for nineteen non-Finkelstein arrays. Bar-end numbers count substitutions; the right column counts distinct substrate pairs within each array. Counts of pairs are not additive across arrays. The retained source corpus contains 410,587 records in twenty tables after 396 exclusions; the nineteen arrays shown contain 406,909 records.

Extended_Data_Figure_2.title: The larger local budget retains a fixed sixteen-profile population
Extended_Data_Figure_2.legend: Original local-update curves for the separate fixed population of 22,963 queries supporting sixteen local profiles. Budgets are 0, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 profiles; the horizontal axis gives the profile count and, below it, the minimum–maximum number of endpoint wells. The curves use equal-group, edge-balanced weighting and the history-only reference. One complete profile contains two reagent endpoints in each included recipe background. Values show changes relative to history alone, without refitting the models.

Extended_Data_Figure_3.title: Calibration between libraries usually worsens the target-only baseline
Extended_Data_Figure_3.legend: All seventeen fixed-support, scored transfers between libraries. Each line follows one direction from target-only prediction to calibrated transfer and the source-identity reassignment control. Errors are normalized to the target-only error for that direction. Calibration worsens fifteen directions (red) and improves two (teal). The source difference channel, budget of 192 and fixed target support follow the original cross-library analysis.

Extended_Data_Figure_4.title: Structure-based prediction primarily recovers each pair's own response level
Extended_Data_Figure_4.legend: This structure-only task excludes both partner molecules from training and is distinct from the two-reference-well learning task in Figure 3. **a**, Two measured response vectors from the substitution with the most supported complete vectors in the three-group decomposition; the displayed pairs have the minimum and maximum own mean response within that population. Solid lines show responses across backgrounds; dashed lines show each pair's own mean. **b**, Error removed within each layer, divided by that layer's centroid-baseline error, for the three-group, group-and-edge-balanced comparison. Approximately 5.0% of pair-level error and 0.22% of background-fluctuation error are removed. **c**, Pair-level (blue) and fluctuation (teal) contributions to net total improvement for two or three groups and three weightings. Each pair's own level accounts for 91.1–96.6% of net improvement. This share uses a different denominator from panel b.

Extended_Data_Figure_5.title: A representative matched-reference comparison illustrates direction and magnitude separately
Extended_Data_Figure_5.legend: **a**, Replacing PdCl₂(dtbpf) with XPhos Pd G3 gives opposite responses in the K₃PO₄ reference and Cs₂CO₃ target backgrounds of the same substrate pair. Target wells were withheld from prediction. **b**, Copying predicts −10.5 percentage points, learning +5.6 points and the measured target change is +34.4 points. Learning identifies the direction but underestimates its magnitude. The predeclared rule requires a reference change of at least 10 points, a measured target change of at least 20 points, an incorrect copied sign and a correct learned sign, plus four retained measured endpoints. The nested eligible pools contain zero flagship-catalyst, 136 Suzuki and 529 total comparisons. The selected Suzuki comparison is nearest the median absolute learned error; lexical identities resolve ties.

Extended_Data_Figure_6.title: Additional molecular changes reshape reagent preferences
Extended_Data_Figure_6.legend: **a**, All sixteen measured yields for acid fluorination and two anilines. Activator and additive are each 1.5 equiv in DMF at 25 °C for 2 h, without base. **b**, FDPP-to-TOTU response contrasts between primary aryl and primary alkyl amines within 42 common acid partners; the red line marks their mean of 33.87 pp. **c**, NMM-to-DIPEA difference-in-differences: the response for 4-methoxybenzylamine minus that for benzylamine over the same eight acids. Points are acids and red ticks their means.

Extended_Data_Figure_7.title: Measured response differences and local information contribute differently
Extended_Data_Figure_7.legend: **a**, Information added by the observed reference difference D beyond mean reference activity S, expressed as the intended-swap improvement minus the matched different-swap improvement in each screen. The pair-held-out, full-history, context-balanced complete-panel population is retained. **b**, Fixed-operator label-content contrasts for Buchwald–Hartwig and Ullmann reactions separate local level and fluctuation information. Negative changes reduce error; the Ullmann fluctuation contrast is near zero.

Extended_Data_Figure_8.title: Combining reaction scopes can require a yield sacrifice
Extended_Data_Figure_8.legend: **a**, Best measured route bottlenecks for two Suzuki scopes separately and after combining them on identical native support. The bracket marks the 13.48 pp yield sacrifice. **b**, Exact Pareto frontier between amide source-scope sacrifice and target-scope bottleneck. The dashed line marks 20% target yield; a source-scope sacrifice of at least 5.00 pp is required to reach it. Displayed values use two decimals; sacrifices are calculated before rounding. The routes use measured recipes.
